question: What is the price tolerance for an invoice line where the unit price is higher than the PO?
gold: The excess on the line must be no more than the lower of 1% of the PO line value and ₹500.
answer_text:
Status: answered
Decision: Tolerance is the lower of 1% of PO line value and ₹500 per line
Answer: When the invoice unit price is higher than the PO unit price, the line passes only if the total excess on that line is no more than the lower of 1% of the PO line value and ₹500. [1] If the excess exceeds that tolerance, the line is held with exception PRICE_VAR and sent to the PO buyer, who must either amend the PO or request a credit note from the supplier. [1][2] PRICE_VAR exceptions must be resolved within 3 working days. [2]
Older sources (superseded): ₹1,000 (AP SOP v3.1); ₹1,000 (Part F); 2% (AP SOP v3.1); 2% (Part F)
judge_reason: The answer states the exact tolerance rule from the gold answer: the lower of 1% of PO line value and ₹500 per line, and adds correct procedural detail without contradiction.

question: Is there a quantity tolerance when the invoice quantity is above the GRN?
gold: No, except the Arvana Infra bulk-material tolerance in client memo CM-INF-02.
answer_text:
Status: answered
Decision: No general tolerance; only Arvana Infra Projects has a 5% tolerance for four bulk materials with a ₹25,000 value cap.
Answer: Under the general rule, invoice quantity must not exceed the GRN quantity and there is no quantity tolerance for any client. [1] The only exception is the bulk-material tolerance agreed with Arvana Infra Projects in Client Memo CM-INF-02. [1] For Arvana Infra Projects, cement, reinforcement steel, sand, and aggregates may be invoiced up to 5% above the GRN quantity provided the excess value on the invoice does not exceed ₹25,000. [2] If the invoice quantity exceeds the GRN quantity (or exceeds the 5%/₹25,000 limits for Arvana's four bulk materials), the exception code QTY_VAR must be raised. [3][2]

question: Above what turnover must a supplier issue an e-invoice with an IRN?
gold: Aggregate annual turnover above ₹5 crore in any financial year since 2017-18.
answer_text:
Status: answered
Decision: Above ₹5 crore aggregate annual turnover
Answer: A supplier whose aggregate annual turnover (AATO) in any financial year since 2017-18 has exceeded ₹5 crore must issue an e-invoice with an Invoice Reference Number (IRN) and QR code. [1] If such a supplier sends an invoice without an IRN, the invoice is not valid for input tax credit and is returned with the exception code IRN_MISSING. [1][2] The base value of an invoice missing an IRN must not be paid; a valid e-invoice will follow. [1]

question: Which GST return is used to decide whether input tax credit can be claimed?
gold: GSTR-2B, generated on the 14th of the following month.
answer_text:
Status: answered
Decision: GSTR-2B is the return used to decide ITC eligibility
